maya (PM): quick sync — customer ACME asked for early access to Optimize toolkit. they want batching, KV caching, and a quant recommendation by pilot. how much can we promise?
thomas (Eng): +1 on scope question. for pilot we can do adaptive batching + a soft KV prefix cache. full KV snapshotting is heavier.
rachel (SRE): we need an SLO baseline. what are acceptance thresholds? p99 latency budget, tail errors, and cost uplift tolerances.
maya (PM): aim: p99 <= 350ms for 1k qps pilot slice, <10% token-cost increase vs current baseline. if quant reduces quality by >3% on eval set, it fails.
joseph (ML): for quantization we can offer two graded recs: 8-bit (fast, some quality risk) and 4-bit w/ per-model calibration (higher engineering cost). we should include an eval gate per prompt set.
sam (ProdOps): rollout constraints: we can start with 10% traffic on Dedicated capacity and auto-roll back to host model on regressions. need clear telemetry events to trigger rollback.
maya (PM): okay — let's draft a minimal pilot acceptance checklist. thomas can you sketch the checklist items?
thomas (Eng): sure. quick draft:
```
- Functional: batching enabled end-to-end for model X
- Cache: prefix cache active for repeated prefixes, eviction LRU
- Quant: 8-bit and calibrated 4-bit variants available
- Telemetry: per-request token cost, model variant tag, latencies, and eval-concordance metrics
- Rollout: canary to 10% -> 30% -> 100% with auto-fallback on eval/regressions
- Test: run eval suite on 5 customer prompt sets, pass quality thresholds
```
maya (PM): nice. add a gating rule for eval-triggered alerts: if quality drop >2% on any prioritized prompt set OR customer-facing NPS dip -> rollback.
joseph (ML): note: we need automated A/B eval harness that runs in prod-like conditions. else alerts will be noisy. i can ship a lightweight runner in 2 sprints.
rachel (SRE): we also need an operational playbook for cache storms and cold-start latencies. include circuit-breaker thresholds.
sam (ProdOps): ops notes: surface a per-customer control to opt-out of quantized variants. legal/regulatory customers will require that.
maya (PM): prioritization question: do we ship batching+caching first and then quant recs, or parallel? customer wants everything but limited eng bandwidth. thoughts?
thomas (Eng): engineering prefers phased: 1) batching + prefixes cache (low risk), 2) quant variants + calibration (higher risk). gives us stable metrics early.
joseph (ML): agree — doing quant in parallel risks destabilizing rollout. but we should prototype quant pipelines now.
maya (PM): decision log: phase 1 = batching + KV prefix cache + eval harness + rollout automation. phase 2 = quant recommendation engine + per-customer opt-out + extended evals.
launch-bot: Created epic OPT-3141: "Fastpath Optimize Pilot — Phase 1" and linked PRD. :rocket:
sam (ProdOps): next steps: schedule stakeholder demo with ACME, get pilot dataset and prompt sets, confirm Dedicated capacity window for 4/12 - 4/26.
maya (PM): assigning owners: thomas -> infra & rollout automation, joseph -> eval harness & quant prototype, rachel -> SLOs & playbook, sam -> pilot ops coordination. i'll follow up with timelines. :thumbsup:
thomas (Eng): note: need a tiny config flag `optimize.fastpath.cache_enabled` to control experiments. will add to CLI and console toggle.
maya (PM): thanks all — i'll post the condensed acceptance checklist and timeline after this thread. if anyone has must-have constraints for pilot, flag them now.
joseph (ML): must-have: a stable seed for eval runs and recording of model logits for repro.
rachel (SRE): must-have: alerting hook to #incidents and a runbook link.
sam (ProdOps): must-have: per-tenant safelist for quant opt-out.
maya (PM): got it — closing for now, will open a follow-up with the concrete schedule.
